Watch the next episode of Jet Lag right now on Nebula: https://nebula.tv/videos/jetlag-ep-3-we-raced-to-visit-the-most-us-states-in-100-hours
Get $20 off an annual Nebula subscription by signing up at http://go.nebula.tv/jetlag

This season, follow Adam and Ben versus Sam and Brian as they travel across the country competing for control over the most US states. They’ll have 4 days to travel to as many states as possible, complete challenges from their deck, and desperately try to defend their territory from this season’s newest twist: battles.

Our other channels:
Wendover Productions - http://youtube.com/wendoverproductions
Half as Interesting - http://youtube.com/halfasinteresting

Follow us on Twitter: http://twitter.com/wendoverpro

Created by Adam Chase, Sam Denby, and Ben Doyle
Editing by Adam Chase, Ben Doyle, Henry Ariza, Ryan Alva
Motion Graphics by Lili Pereira, Max Moser, Josh Sherrington, Maddy Haynes, Sara Stoltman, Aelee Vang, Derek Brown, Mikaila Blackburn, Neel Sawant, Parker Simmons
Audio by Manni Simon, Donovan Bullen
Supervising Producer Graham Haerther
Artwork by Simon Buckmaster

This is it...The 100,000 Subscriber Special is here! This, my beautiful Beard Army, is THE 100,000 CALORIE CHALLENGE! 

The rules are simple...100 hours to eat 100,000 calories! 

NOTES, FAQs & NUTRITIONAL INFORMATION:

First, let me say a big hairy 'thank you' to each and every subscriber out there! I've said it before, and I'm sure I'll say it again, but it means the world to me that you continue to support the channel and help it grow. Whether you've been around since 100 subs, 1000 subs, or you were the 100,000th, I really do appreciate it!

Second, after The 35,000 Calorie Cheat Day and The 50,000 Calorie Challenge, I never thought I'd lose my marbles enough to try something even more insane...But overwhelmingly, looking through the comments, I noticed that a 100,000 calorie challenge was overwhelmingly what people wanted. Whether possible or not, I thought I owed it to you guys to at least try!

Third, I've done this kind of thing for a long time now. So I'm used to people saying what I do is fake, that calorie counts are exaggerated or that because the video is edited, it never happened. That's fine, everyone on the planet is entitled to their opinion, but if you have your doubts, then at least do me the courtesy of reading the FAQs and nutritional information at the bottom of the description before commenting.

FAQs:

Q: Why aren't you fat? A: Exercise and calorie control. Although believe me, after this one, fat gain is inevitable.

Q: Why is the video cut and edited? A: All of my videos are cut/edited with multiple angles, crops and effects, whereby the eating occurs in time with the music and to create drama and entertainment. Although in this case, it's mostly to get as much of the eating, emotion and fun in as possible. Before anyone suggests it, no a 100 hour unedited YouTube video is not possible.

Q: Where do you get the calorie/nutritional information from? A: All calorie content is estimated to the best of my ability, using nutritional labels, MyFitnessPal or prevailing caloric standards/website nutritional PDFs. More detailed information can be found below.

Q: Will you ever do it again? A: Only if I ever reach 1 million subscribers, which I highly doubt will ever happen.

Ordinarily, I'm not one for the chugging...I leave that kinda stuff to Badlands...but it's not often you come across quirky challenges over here, so when I heard about Bake, Battle & Roll's Five Shake Challenge, I had to give it a crack.

Now the rules for this one are pretty unique. It costs £15 to order five rich ice cream shakes of your choice from their menu. If you manage to sink them all faster than the current record time, then they're on the house and you get a winner's certificate for your trouble. You are allowed to let them melt prior to starting and you can stir the shakes as much as you like before your first gulp. You also have to keep the shakes down for 30 minutes after consumption.

The record stood for a while at a respectable 12 minutes. That was until some savage by the name of Daniel came along and bashed five in an impressive 1.45. Daniel was smart...he ordered five strawberry shakes...but this ain't amateur hour...so I'm throwing down against two strawberry, two chocolate and one delicious biscoff!

NFWfTMwIV_Y.description:
Here it is folks! Hello and welcome to The One Million Subscriber Special! Let me take another opportunity to say thank you once more for helping me to reach such an incredible milestone. I doubt that I’ll ever be able to repay the debt that I owe to each of you, but hopefully this video goes some way to making that gesture. 

Now if you’re thinking of commenting, I’d appreciate it if you’d take a few seconds to read through a few points I’d like to make, since I know that as always there are likely to be plenty of people with questions. As well as some who may be disappointed, upset or just unhappy with what I did to mark the occasion. 

First, just bear in mind that this being a one million subscriber land mark video; the hype that comes with that notion means it was always likely to underwhelm people to some degree. What I wanted to do was to explore something I’d never done before, which I thought would engage as many people as possible and make for an entertaining video. 

Second, to the people who are disappointed that it’s not ‘The One Million Calorie Challenge’, ‘200,000 Calorie Challenge’ or even a reattempt of The 100,000 Calorie Challenge in 100 hours that I tried all those years ago. Please try to consider that if like me you make YouTube videos for over five years, not only does the type of content you make change, but your mentality and responsibilities change too. 

One of the reasons I very rarely do ‘cheat days’ or ‘calorie challenges’ these days is because, quite simply, I don’t enjoy them. They’ve been done to death. I find them difficult to appreciate, and as a result difficult to turn into a cohesive, entertaining video which people can have fun watching. That being said, people often ask for them, so I try to do them from time to time for special occasions etc. but never at the expense of other videos I have planned. Moreover, with time not only has my content changed, my personal and professional responsibilities have too. So whereas many years ago I could dedicate 100 hours of filming and just as many in editing to one video, now I simply can’t given what I have to do in my day to day life as a 35 year old. 

Finally, whether you enjoy the video or hate it. At the very least, please accept that the idea I came up with and tried to execute was born out of the desire to do something most people would enjoy. That is to say, something which involves the subscribers that got me to where I am. So whether you like or loath it; know that I did my best and with the best intentions. Of course there are things I would change to improve it, but again keep in mind that filming something this ambitious, as a one man band with no filming crew etc. is no easy task. Especially when so much of the concept of the video is outside of the creator’s control.

As I mentioned at the end of the video, I’m taking a week off now. Doing what I do, and doing it in a way different to which many other similar creators do it, is of course very physically demanding. And I promised myself some time ago a week off to rest, rejuvenate and of course plan for future. So there’ll be no mid-week video, but you can rest assured I’ve got something for you this time next Sunday at 7pm BST as always. 

Thanks for watching, I hope you enjoy it and as always I’m in your debt. Lots of love, BMF :)

***NEW VIDEOS EVERY THURSDAY AND SUNDAY AT 7PM GMT***

ANSWERS TO COMMON QUESTIONS & ADDITIONAL INFO:

Q: How come you don’t get fat? 
A: I eat like this for 1 hour of a 168 hour long week. In simple terms, I eat at caloric maintenance over the course of time, meaning I don’t gain weight. If you're interested in learning more, see the 'It Was Just A Normal Day...' video.

Q: Don’t you worry about your health?
A: Not in particular. I’m active. I eat nutrient dense foods five days a week. And, I get quarterly bloods done, amongst other health checks.

cCRrsekZ210.description:
The cringe is strong with this one...But I thought it'd be a laugh nonetheless! People often ask me to do full 'normal day of eating' videos...But, as I mentioned in last Tuesday's bonus episode, a 'normal' day of eating for me pretty much consists of one tuna salad. That's it.

So I thought it might be fun to take a step back in time and try to eat my entire daily diet back when I was at my heaviest bodyweight!

POINTS TO NOTE:

1) The diet I was following at this specific point was for a short period only before returning to a more modest intake of around 3500 calories per day. The pictures included for reference do not perfectly reflect my condition/composition at the precise time, they're just the closest photos I had to hand (I don't have a huge collection).
2) I am not advocating that anyone try follow this as a diet regimen. I simple thought it would be fun to show the kind of things I ate around 7 years ago at my heaviest body weight, when I was even more active than I am now and had goals orientated towards hypertrophy.
3) As you get older, your priorities change. So for those of you wondering why I don't look like this now, it's because I have better things to do with my time than exercise for hours every day and constantly over eat, all to simply look a certain way. It was a pursuit I enjoyed for a time, but now I exercise purely for practical levels of strength and optimal health.

Day two in Georgia and we're heading to a little town called Tucker to take on a not so little burger challenge...

Named after the American folkloric hero John Henry, this burger consists of 7 half pound beef patties, 7 slices of bacon and 7 slices of cheese, an egg on top and accompanied by a pound of fries. Finish it inside one hour and the meal is FREE, in addition to a t-shirt, a cap or a hoodie...and a commemorative railroad spike...

With only two victors to date (one looking remarkably similar to me) I'm wondering if there's a catch. One way to find out...

QcTCvv72l6M.description:
I thought for a little change of pace this week it might be a larf to have a bash at taking down my entire daily diet back from when I was hugely overweight as a child. Clearly I didn't quite grasp at the time just how much I was eating!

I've been reading a lot about so-called initiatives to tackle childhood obesity recently; sugar taxes, banning fast food advertisements, but very little in the way of simply educating people as to how energy turnover works in the human body. And that's really the solution to the problem. As well as being a bit of fun, I thought it might be interesting to demonstrate just how easy it is to severely over eat without necessarily realising it in the short term.

I'm not the preachy type, but if you want to manage your weight effectively then the best way to do it is to track your caloric intake over time. If you over do it one day, then make sure you under do it the next. Oh and don't eat giant blocks of madeira cake when you're bored ;)

A few weeks back I mentioned making a GIANT Belgian Bun...Well, today is that day...

9lb and over 11,000 calories of every self-respecting patisserie lover's favourite iced snack...But can it be eaten by one man?

RECIPE:

1600g plain flour
1 litre milk
150g butter
8 tablespoons of sugar
2 packets fast-acting yeast
3 eggs
350g lemon curd
300g currents/raisins/sultanas
400g icing sugar

METHOD:

Mix dry ingredients. Add wet ingredients. Mix. Turn out onto a floured surface. Knead for ten minutes. Cover in a bowl with clingfilm until mixture has doubled in size. Cut into strips. Spread lemon curd and raisins. Roll into one giant wheel. Bake on 160 fan for 90-120 minutes. Ice. Top with a cherry ;)

Q: How are you going to keep making videos?
A: Things are going to be different for a little while for sure, but I think now more than ever it's important to try to put out videos that people enjoy. It's going to be an adjustment, but I've got plans and I'm confident I can still make some enjoyable stuff despite limitations on travel etc.

Q: How can you get food?
A: The way I see it, there's an opportunity to contribute to local restaurants that have moved to delivery-only services, in addition to limiting the necessity to shop for food in public. A common sense approach to creating videos is of course is the way to go, and if we all shop for conveniences responsibly, current supply chains are robust and equipped enough to deal with perfectly adequate food provisions.

For the next few weeks at least, things are of course going to change a little, but if there's ever a time I feel compelled to create new content it's now, so I'm gonna do my best to keep the content rolling while lock-down is in effect.

DISCLAIMER: All the food in today's video was ordered via contactless delivery from a local Italian restaurant; details of which can be found below if you're interested. This conforms with current social distancing measures. Any suggestions to the contrary in the comments thread will not receive a response.

Restaurant: @Valentinos.Wakefield

In answer to general questions regarding current social restrictions and the impact this has on the channel, please see below:

Q: How are you going to keep making videos?
A: Things are going to be different for a little while for sure, but I think now more than ever it's important to try to put out videos that people enjoy. It's going to be an adjustment, but I've got plans and I'm confident I can still make some enjoyable stuff despite limitations on travel etc.

Q: How can you get food?
A: The way I see it, there's an opportunity to contribute to local restaurants that have moved to delivery-only services, in addition to limiting the necessity to shop for food in public. This isn't about scoring brownie points, but it does provide a useful and mutually beneficial solution to the problems posed by current necessary social restrictions.

Q: Isn't doing this right now distasteful?
A: Though I can see the reason for the question, I disagree. Given that I maintain both my bodyweight and health by eating in an extreme caloric deficit on the days of the week I'm not filming, I'm well versed in not eating more than I require over time. It's how I do what I do while remaining in good health. That said, of course I'm not going to walk into my local store and buy 16 loaves of bread. A common sense approach to creating videos is of course is the way to go, and if we all shop for conveniences responsibly, current supply chains are robust and equipped enough to deal with perfectly adequate food provisions.
